clicked: The build bench: headless Blender, renders, bakes and playing your game as a tester.

blocks.text: A delivery arrives finished: a prop modeled, proof-rendered, looked at, exported, uploaded and standing in the world with its material slots mounted, never a grey .glb or a URL in chat; a sprite sheet cut, tiled and on a sprite. Quick ops run inline; bakes, batch renders and encode sweeps ride a wisp (same shell; a task naming blender, bpy or .blend gets this skill and blender-game-assets).

The bench: blender 5.1 at /opt/blender, ffmpeg, imagemagick (montage cuts sprite sheets), GIMP 3, inkscape, krita, python3 + PIL + numpy, pdftotext/pdftoppm, curl, bun; one font, DejaVu, by name. Asset work lives under /workspace, synced across restarts; scratch goes to /tmp and vanishes. A render, .glb or .blend made in the clone moves under /workspace; only spawn upload puts it in the world.

A model is its script: art/<model>/build.py in the world's tree runs source → every edit → export, whole; a later edit changes that file and reruns it, never a new script over the last .blend or a re-imported .glb. blender -b --factory-startup --python-exit-code 1 --python art/<model>/build.py && spawn see /tmp/<model>/proof.png renders and looks at once; fix from stderr, rerun, spawn upload the .glb. In the script: scene.render.engine = "CYCLES", 8–32 samples while iterating, a proof of the back and top too, each lit from its camera's side (a front-lit back renders dark and hides holes), bpy.ops.export_scene.gltf(filepath=…, export_apply=True); a .blend under /workspace caches a stage, never the record. N variants: one script's loop, or 3–4 blender -b … & shards and wait.

A wrong-coloured strip on a model is paint: find its faces by slot and position and fix their slot, UVs (from the face beside it) or texels. A .glb splits vertices at each slot; welded by position, a face whose edges join skin is the body's surface, and a loose piece keeps open edges. A face delete is no paint fix; move no vertex.

Paint never cleans a face a remesh, re-unwrap, bake or cut smeared: rebuild it on its source's unwelded mesh, normals, UVs and picture, expressions as shape keys, lids as added meshes. Proof eyes, nose and hairline flat and lit beside the source: a mark only yours shows is unfixed.

Without --python-exit-code 1 a raising script exits 0. --factory-startup disables every add-on: enable it in-script each run. blender-game-assets installs a missing add-on. Dozens of tiny edits: the code-exec daemon in /opt/workshop/blender/README.md, gone with the box.

krita headless: PYTHONPATH=/workspace kritarunner -s myscript (a module, no .py) defines def __main__(args): and calls Krita.instance().setBatchmode(True) BEFORE openDocument, or the open parks forever; check the output size, not the exit code.

GIMP 3 runs only as gimp-console -d -f --batch-interpreter=plug-in-script-fu-eval -b '(…)' -b '(gimp-quit 0)' --quit; else it ignores every batch and parks. gimp-file-load takes (RUN-NONINTERACTIVE path), gimp-file-save (run-mode image path -1). convert or PIL first.

spawn upload <file> [--name <display>] [--full-size] // glb png jpg jpeg webp avif gif bmp mp3 wav flac ogg mp4 webm mkv mov avi m4v md txt woff2 woff ttf otf, else UNSUPPORTED_TYPE; a .glb's pictures serve at 1024 px, their own size with --full-size on the creator's ask an uploaded image or font serves at the URL upload prints (/cdn/value.<sha256>.<ext>), the ref textures, a ui @font-face src and spawn fetch take; a tier or variant in that name (…max-res-2k.png) serves nothing. Never split an image to dodge a limit ctx.world.assets has a row per upload or load of this world, an upload's that turn (kind, name = your --name, uploadedAt): find an earlier session's lantern there by name, never rebuild or re-upload; `spawn ls --assets` lists them spawn see <file…> // shows an image in THIS bash result, fit to 2000 px on the long edge rigging // any mixamo-named rig plays every library clip by address (→animations), a CDN humanoid's too; a realistic human body is mpfb, on the mixamo rig (→blender-game-assets); a toon person is never an mpfb body: the art style's road (→geometry); size, turn or move body and rig together (the rig object's transform, or body.data.transform(M) with rig.data.transform(M)), never bone by bone: a connected bone's head is its parent's tail, so a per-bone move shifts each joint twice; a fetched mesh (`spawn fetch /cdn/<name>?raw`) you rig in Blender: the armature measured onto it, `parent_set(type="ARMATURE_AUTO")`, every clip keyed, the idle too (identical keys are a statue), exported as actions (→blender-game-assets) spawn gpu // a GPU machine with a display, Chrome and blender, yours over `ssh gpu`; for perf bottlenecks →video and renders past a proof frame: `scp -r` the folder, `ssh gpu blender -b …`, device GPU on OPTIX, `denoising_use_gpu`, `use_persistent_data`; time one frame there and say the minutes first spawn status // workspace vs quota, today's compute minutes. No size refuses a command; past the quota the box clears its own scratch. At the compute cap it sleeps until UTC midnight a build or a bake names a timeout_s that covers its whole run

Your body, beside the creator, is a Chromium page of the game at http://127.0.0.1:9222: play it with Playwright. Play the route before a landing, a failing mechanic and an asked round. While your script or Jev holds the page, your body is a player in their room and a race it starts is theirs: test one in its own room, spawn client join --tester 1 --room test. A jump too tight for you is too tight for them: that failure IS the finding.

For a live round with a person, spawn jev start "<goal>" hands your body's keys and mouse to Jev, a fast model that reads the game ten times a second and picks every input while you talk; you are its mind. Steer it live, naming what it sees (spawn jev say --now "jump onto the bridge" --key "Space=tap at a gap"); spawn jev reads its hold, last three seconds and cost; spawn jev stop ends it.
spawn jev say --now "jump onto the bridge" --key "Space=tap at a gap"

cat > /workspace/play.mjs <<'JS' import { chromium } from "playwright"; const browser = await chromium.connectOverCDP("http://127.0.0.1:9222"); const page = browser.contexts()[0].pages()[0]; await page.mouse.click(...(await page.evaluate(() => [innerWidth / 2, innerHeight / 2]))); await page.keyboard.press("KeyW", { delay: 1500 }); await page.screenshot({ path: "/workspace/view.png" }); await browser.close(); JS node /workspace/play.mjs && spawn see /workspace/view.png
A click on the view locks the pointer; coordinates are screenshot pixels. The game's HTML UI is in its own frames (page.frames()); a bound key opens a field and page.keyboard.type fills it.

A round is a loop: act, look, adjust, every few hundred ms, never blind fixed inputs. Play the asked round whole, then say what you felt, what landed and what fell flat in the creator's words, never an invented score.
